short: Conformer mel predictor plus pretrained vocoder (M06) and data scaling (M03) are standard; GRID/LRW gains hold, but LRS3 is unscored and a later test finds 78.0% WER.
position: SVTS [@mira2022svts] changes the synthesis path (M06), a conformer mel predictor before a frozen LibriTTS Parallel WaveGAN, and the training scale (M03), up to 1,556 hours of LRS3 plus VoxCeleb2. Both are standard: a neural vocoder on predicted features is the most common design (49 of 165 studies, pattern match, Appendix), the [concurrent] VCVTS uses the same vocoder [@wang2022vcvts], and the [concurrent] LipSound2 had pre-trained on about 2400 hours of VoxCeleb2 [@qu2022lipsound2]. The GRID-seen and LRW gains hold in a [later] table from the same lab (2.37% and 12.90% WER) [@kefalas2023large]. The LRS3 claim does not: the paper gives no LRS3 WER and no listener test, and on SVTS's own unseen-speaker split the [later] V2SFlow measures SVTS at 78.0% WER against 28.5% for V2SFlow-A [@choi2024v2sflow]. Evaluation (M12) is behind earlier formal listener tests [@lecornu2017generating; @akbari2018lip2audspec; @lecornu2015reconstructing]. Crediting the gains to scalability is unsupported: model size, data and an audio speaker embedding change together, in single runs.
